# Context Menu

> Menu's Menu Items, opened where the user right-clicks or long-presses, or from the keyboard, in place of the browser's own menu.

`<slab-context-menu>` · Navigation · built on `[role=menu] + [popover]`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/context-menu/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/context-menu.js';
import 'slab-elements/menu.item.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-context-menu label="File">
  <div slot="target" tabindex="0">Right-click me</div>

  <slab-menu-item>Rename</slab-menu-item>
  <slab-menu-item>Duplicate</slab-menu-item>
  <slab-menu-item disabled>Delete</slab-menu-item>
</slab-context-menu>
```

To do something when a Menu Item is chosen, listen for its "click". Make the target focusable, or put something focusable in it, so the keyboard can open the menu too. Prevent the default of a "contextmenu" in part of the target to keep the menu from opening there.

On iOS, a long-press on text also starts selecting it. Give the target `user-select: none` if that gets in the way.

## Keyboard

| Key             | What it does                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Shift+F10, Menu | In the target, opens the menu below what has focus, at the first Menu Item.   |
| Up, Down        | Moves to the previous or next Menu Item, wrapping and skipping disabled ones. |
| Home, End       | Moves to the first or last Menu Item.                                         |
| A character     | Moves to the next Menu Item whose label starts with what's typed.             |
| Enter, Space    | Clicks the active Menu Item and closes the menu.                              |
| Escape          | Closes the menu and returns focus to where it was.                            |
| Tab             | Closes the menu and moves focus on.                                           |

## Elements

### `<slab-context-menu>`

Import `slab-elements/context-menu.js` to register it.

A context menu with no visual styles: a list of Menu Items that opens over whatever is slotted into `target`, where the user asks for it, in place of the browser's own.

It opens on a right-click, and on Control-click on a Mac, at the pointer. It opens on a long-press with a finger or a pen too, where it was pressed. And it opens on Shift+F10 or the Menu key, below whatever in the target has focus. The browser's menu doesn't open for any of them. A "contextmenu" whose default a consumer has already prevented is left alone, so a part of the target, or a Context Menu nested in it, can have a menu of its own.

Its Menu Items are Menu's, in a `[role=menu]` element in a native `[popover]`, and the keyboard is Menu's. Focus moves to the menu while it's open, and its `aria-activedescendant` points at the active Menu Item. The Up and Down arrows move through the Menu Items, wrapping and skipping disabled ones, Home and End go to the first and last, and typing moves to the next one whose label starts with what was typed. Hovering a Menu Item makes it the active one. Enter, Space and a click click the Menu Item and close the menu. Escape and Tab close it, Escape returning focus to where it was.

It's kept on screen, opening up or back from the pointer when there isn't room below or after it, as the operating system's do.

Style it through its parts and `:state(open)`, and each Menu Item through the states Menu Item sets.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                    |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names the menu.                                |
| `open`             | `boolean` | `false` | Whether it's open. Set it to open or close it. |

#### Properties

| Name                | Type         | Description               |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------- |
| `items` (read-only) | `MenuItem[]` | Its Menu Items, in order. |

#### Methods

| Signature                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hide(): void`                                    | Closes it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `show(position?: { x: number; y: number }): void` | Opens the menu at `x` and `y`, in the viewport's coordinates, or below whatever in the target has focus when they're left out.                                                                                                                                |
| `toggle(force?: boolean): boolean`                | Opens it when it's closed, below whatever in the target has focus, and closes it when it's open, as a native popover's `togglePopover()` does. `true` only opens it, without moving it when it's open, and `false` only closes it. Returns whether it's open. |

#### Events

| Name           | Type          | Description                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toggle`       | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does. |
| `beforetoggle` | `ToggleEvent` | Before it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` that doesn't bubble. Cancel it while it's opening to keep it closed.   |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                    | Description                                                    |
| --------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`  | `Element`               | Where a right-click, a long-press, or Shift+F10 opens the menu |
| (default) | `MenuItem \| MenuGroup` |                                                                |

#### CSS parts

| Name      | Description            |
| --------- | ---------------------- |
| `menu`    | The Menu Items         |
| `popover` | What the menu opens in |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's open. |

### `<slab-menu-item>`

Import `slab-elements/menu.item.js` to register it.

A Menu Item with no visual styles. The host is the menu item, so style it directly.

Listen for "click" on it to act on it. Its Menu clicks it for Enter and Space, the way a button is clicked from the keyboard, and closes once it has. A disabled Menu Item isn't clicked, again like a button.

`type="checkbox"` makes it a `menuitemcheckbox`, which a click checks or unchecks. `type="radio"` makes it a `menuitemradio`, which a click checks, unchecking the other radio Menu Items beside it. Put each set of radios in a Menu Group, so they're named together and kept apart from the rest. Either way, it's checked or unchecked before any "click" listener hears the click, as a native checkbox is, so a listener reads the new `checked`.

It's never focused. Focus stays on its Menu, which points at the active Menu Item with `aria-activedescendant`.

Its Menu sets `:state(active)`. It sets `:state(checked)` and `:state(disabled)` itself. Nothing is drawn for a check: that's a mark a design makes.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type                              | Default  | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label`    | `string`                          |          | Names the Menu Item in place of its text, and is what typeahead matches against.                                              |
| `checked`  | `boolean`                         | `false`  | Whether a checkbox or radio Menu Item is checked. Ignored for any other.                                                      |
| `disabled` | `boolean`                         | `false`  | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted. |
| `type`     | `'checkbox' \| 'item' \| 'radio'` | `'item'` | "checkbox" for an item that's checked and unchecked, "radio" for one that's checked within its Menu Group, or "item".         |

#### Properties

| Name               | Type     | Description                                                                               |
| ------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text` (read-only) | `string` | What the user reads as the Menu Item's name: its label, or its text when it has no label. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                                                |
| --------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | The label, plus anything else a design puts in a Menu Item |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(active)`   | While it's the active one, which the keyboard moves through while focus stays on its container. |
| `:state(checked)`  | While it's checked.                                                                             |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                            |
